why: placid (calm, not easily excited) is a near-opposite of fervent
tumultuous ('not calm at all') is an opposite of placid
palpable ('obvious') is a near-opposite of insidious (ant: obvious)
decidedly ('definitely') matches ant 'definitely'; vehemently is a near-opposite
tentatively is a near-opposite of vehemently
escalate (syn 'worsen') matches rectify's antonym 'worsen'
eradicate (end completely) is a near-opposite of perpetuate (ant: end, stop)
hinder is a near-opposite of nurture (encourage growth)
quell (calm, put an end to unrest) is a near-opposite of exacerbate (ant: ease, relieve)
oblivious is a near-opposite of astute/perceptive
'easily' and 'fully' are forced opposites of scarcely; no true antonym
'suppress' is not a genuine opposite of evoke
'hesitant' is not an opposite of adamant (firm, unwilling to change mind)
'hold' in this sense is not one a learner would recognize as a synonym
'attitude' is an inner stance, not outward manner; not a true synonym
'prohibit' means forbid by rule, a different meaning
'subtle' lacks the harmful sense; not a synonym
'loathsome' is rarer than the headword; 'disgusting' is a recognizable synonym

set.def: belonging only to one person or thing; unusual and highly individual in style

why: plain-word: 'peculiar to' uses a rare sense of 'peculiar' that learners read as 'strange'

set.def: good at finding clever ways to solve problems, especially when money, tools, or help are limited

why: plain-word: 'means' in the sense 'resources' is unclear to learners

set.also: a Christian holiday traditionally held on January 6, twelve days after Christmas (“Many churches hold a special service at Epiphany.”)

why: not always held on Jan 6 (e.g. US Catholic Sunday observance, Julian-calendar churches); add 'traditionally'

set.also: a problem that makes it hard for someone to speak clearly (“He has a mild speech impediment.”)

why: speech impediments (e.g. stuttering) are not always physical
